newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's Rafsanjani expected to visit Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Rafsanjani expected to visit Saudi.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani is expected to make his first official visit to Saudi Arabia in April to perform the haj pilgrimage, Iran's ambassador to Riyadh said in remarks published on Friday.
Mohammad Reza Nouri told the London-based Arabic-language Asharq al-Awsat newspaper that the pilgrimage would mark Rafsanjani's first official visit to Saudi Arabia.
Nouri stressed the importance of the visit, saying it would "strengthen bilateral relations between Saudi Arabia and Iran."
"President Rafsanjani's visit will give a strong push forward to bring the hearts and policies (of the two sides) closer," he said.
Rafsanjani's last travelled to Saudi Arabia at the start of the 1979 Iranian revolution on a personal visit to perform the haj, Nouri said.
Iran's ties with Saudi Arabia, the most influential Gulf country and custodian to Islam's two holiest shrines, have been tense since Iran's revolution.
Tehran has been trying to improve its ties with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Arab states.
Analysts say Iran's desire to improve ties with Riyadh have been reflected by a softer tone used by the media and officials towards Saudi Arabia in the past few weeks.
Riyadh has refused to confirm U.S. media reports of an Iranian link to the June bombing which killed 19 U.S. servicemen in the eastern Saudi city of Khobar.
Iran -- which Washington accuses of sponsoring state terrorism and has imposed snactions on -- denies any role.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said that his visit to Saudi Arabia earlier this month as part of a Gulf tour had opened up a new chapter in relations between Tehran and Riyadh. MG
